title: {Syn} AKS Made Primality Deterministic in Polynomial Time
content:
The AKS primality test, announced in 2002, showed that deciding whether a number is prime can be done deterministically in polynomial time without assuming unproved hypotheses.

Practical systems often use faster probabilistic tests, but AKS mattered because it settled a foundational complexity question with an unconditional answer.

Why it matters: algorithms keeps producing ideas that are simple enough to state and strong enough to build with.
